summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and fluid retention, with a plan to undergo right heart catheterization to assess pulmonary pressures. He had gained weight and required 4L of oxygen at night. Due to thrombocytopenia previously linked to Remodulin, dose escalation was not pursued. He was treated with IV diuresis to reduce fluid overload before the procedure. Right heart catheterization revealed improved pulmonary artery systolic pressure at 38 mm Hg, down from 47 mm Hg, with normal filling pressures and preserved cardiac index. His oxygen requirements remained stable. He was discharged home on unchanged medications, including Remodulin at 45 ng/kg/min, furosemide, amiloride, and other home therapies. He was instructed to monitor weight and follow up with specialty care.
